newsitem.title: USA: Detroit NAPM business index falls to 56.0 in Feb.
newsitem.headline: Detroit NAPM business index falls to 56.0 in Feb.

text.p: The Detroit National Association of Purchasing Management business index for February fell 2.2 points to 56.0, versus 58.2 in January, said Comerica Bank which tabulates the monthly index.

The index is a seasonally-adjusted weighted average measure of new orders and production, as well as employment, inventories and the promptness of supplier deliveries, in both the auto and non-auto sectors of Detroit's economy.
"The principal cause of February's easing was a decline in auto sector production and employment," David Littmann, chief economist with Detroit-based Comerica Bank, said in a news release.
Auto-related production fell to 59.4 in February, from 67.5 in January, while auto-related employment decreased to 58.8, compared to 67.5 in January.

Production for both auto- and non-auto sectors fell to 60.0 in February, from 62.2 in January, while employment for both sectors declined to 51.1, from 60.9. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com))
